summary: A remote install can report success having installed nothing: when _filterDepsForEngine removes every dep from the request, POST /comfy/models/download/start still returns success:true with a 0/0 job that settles to complete. Measured twice on a live Pod during MPI-450's session (dep IDs sent as strings; and a dep belonging to a different tier of the same family), costing two Pod legs. The filter itself is correct - MPI-163/179 added it on purpose - the defect is treating an emptied request as a no-op instead of a caller error. Not a 1.4 gate: pre-existing, not a regression, and the renderer resolves correctly so no user path reaches it. Sweep both engine branches and the uninstall route, which carries the same filter via MPI-276 G13.

Third sighting, 2026-08-10, and it cost another Pod leg. A driver sent dependencies as bare id STRINGS; _filterDepsForEngine filters on d.id, which is undefined for a string, so the set emptied and POST /comfy/models/download/start answered success:true with a 0/0 job that settled to complete while a live Pod sat idle for 2.5 minutes. Three input shapes now reach the same silent no-op: id-string, wrong-tier dep object, wrong-engine dep object - which is the argument for option 1 (422 naming the dropped ids and the engine), since only the response can tell a shape error from an engine mismatch. Added to the brief: the 422 must distinguish 'you sent N deps and all N were dropped' from 'you sent 0 deps', because a 0-dep POST is a legitimate request for nothing.
